_about: Figures ci/mob-tick-census.py derives from the pinned 26.2 jar and from crates/rustmc-server/src/entities.rs. `--check` refuses if any of them moves. Re-pin deliberately: a figure that moved is either a jar change (impossible, it is pinned) or a real change in this workspace, and both deserve a commit message.
_expected_to_move: `our_entity_kinds`, `our_mob_kinds` and `transcription_disagreements` are the only figures here that can move without the jar pin moving. The first two are SUPPOSED to move as work lands and re-pinning them belongs in the same commit as the port; `transcription_disagreements` moving is a defect in crates/rustmc-entity/src/tick.rs and is not a figure to re-pin. Everything else is jar-derived against a pinned jar.
_the_point: ci/unported-inventory.py --open reports 1 entity-behaviour gap. hierarchy_declarations is the size of what that one row stands for.
_transcription: `transcription_disagreements` must stay 0. It compares MobCategory's despawn distances and getNoDespawnDistance as written in crates/rustmc-entity/src/tick.rs against the same values read from the pinned jar. A non-zero here is a real defect in the crate, not a pin that needs moving.
_yaw: `entitytype_nextfloat_sites` is pinned as a LIST, not a count. It is `create@103` — the spawn yaw, drawn from an unseeded generator, and the single cause behind 080's 15/15 floor flap, spawn_mobs measuring as a null, and the standing 4-of-92 corpus floor being entirely entity scenarios. If a second site ever appears, `the spawn yaw draw` stops being a definite article and every sentence built on it has to be re-read.
